subject: Request for redacted penetration test dossier and remediation timeline
messages:
From: Tom Jensen <tom.jensen@mediacorp.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request for pen test dossier and remediation timeline

Vivek,

We've been reviewing telemetry around our integration with Redwood and observed a pattern that looks like anomalous token refreshes correlated to our nightly batch runs. This is incident-adjacent; nothing conclusive on our end yet, but given contract Section 4.2 (security obligations) we need the following urgently:

- A copy of the most recent penetration test report (redacted as needed to protect other customers and PII)
- A short scope summary that lists tested subsystems (auth, api-gateway, storage, etc.) and dates
- Current remediation status for any findings that touch token handling or session management
- Any indicators of compromise (IOCs) or related mitigations you implemented in the last 90 days

We need this information within 48 hours to brief our legal/security team. If you cannot provide a full report, please share an executive summary plus technical addendum with the remediation timeline. Also confirm whether your SOC 2 Type II auditor observed any related exceptions in the same window.

Please CC whoever owns security at Redwood. If you need an NDA or safe-receipt process for unredacted materials, let us know.

Thanks,
Tom Jensen
Head of Security Operations
MediaCorp
From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Jensen <tom.jensen@mediacorp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 07 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request for pen test dossier and remediation timeline

Tom —

Thanks for flagging this and for the clear asks. We take anything incident-adjacent seriously and will prioritize. High-level next steps from our side:

1) Immediate share: we can provide a redacted penetration test executive report and a remediation-status CSV that enumerates findings, severity, and current state. These redactions remove exploit POC, step-by-step reproduction, and any data that would identify other customers.

2) Technical addendum: for high-severity items that affect auth/session/token handling we can provide a redacted technical addendum that includes enough detail on root cause, mitigations applied, and guidance for partner integrations — but still omits exploit code.

3) Compliance artifacts: we will include an excerpt from our SOC 2 Type II report (auditor: Stonebridge Audit LLP) that covers the period that overlaps the pen test window.

Attachments I am sending now (redacted): Redwood_PenTest_Summary_v1_redacted.pdf, SOC2_TypeII_Excerpt_2026.pdf, Remediation_Status_20261107.csv. Please confirm receipt and whether MediaCorp has an NDA on file for receiving less-redacted materials; if not, we can route unredacted artifacts through our secure portal and a mutual NDA process.

If you'd like, Marissa (cc'd) will hop on a call to walk through the findings and remediation plan. We can schedule a technical briefing today or Monday.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Vivek —

Thanks for the quick response and the initial attachments (received). A couple of clarifying questions from our engineering/security leads:

- The executive report is helpful but we need a little more technical granularity on the finding labeled "AUTH-06" in your remediation CSV — specifically whether the vulnerability requires an exploit of token storage vs. token rotation race conditions. Any details you can share without providing PoC would help us model risk.

- For the technical addendum: we can accept redacted technical detail, but we need confirmation that the addendum will include the exact endpoints/paths affected (e.g., /v1/auth/refresh) and the mitigations applied (e.g., rotation window shortened to X seconds, server-side nonce).

- Please confirm the ETA for the addendum and whether your SOC 2 auditor noted any control exceptions in Q3/Q4 2026 related to auth/session management.

This is a high-priority request at MediaCorp — if it's easier, escalate to your security leadership and we'll set a 30-minute bridge.

Tom

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 08 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request for pen test dossier and remediation timeline

Tom —

Appreciate the details. I'm Marissa, Director of InfoSec at Redwood; looping in Aditya from engineering to ensure we capture the exact mitigations. A few points and deliverables from our side: 

- We prepared a technical addendum that enumerates affected endpoints (redacted to path-level; no exploit code). It confirms AUTH-06 relates to a timing/race condition in refresh handling under heavy concurrent requests, not persistent credential exposure. The addendum lists impacted paths (redacted to coarse path: /v1/auth/refresh) and the mitigation applied (server-side token rotation + optimistic locking on refresh operations).

- SOC 2: Our Type II auditor (Stonebridge Audit LLP) did not report exceptions in the auth control family for the period covering Q2–Q3 2026. The SOC excerpt attached includes the control matrix references.

- ETA & process: Attached is the technical addendum (Redwood_PenTest_Technical_Addendum_redacted.pdf). Remaining low-severity items are scheduled for remediation by 2026-11-20; the remediation CSV lists owners and PR numbers. Internal tracking: INC-2026-0145.

- If MediaCorp needs a secure channel for less-redacted materials, we can open a secure transfer under a mutual NDA and restrict access to named recipients. Let me know the recipient list and we'll provision.

Attachments: Redwood_PenTest_Technical_Addendum_redacted.pdf (technical mitigations), Remediation_Status_20261107.csv, SOC2_TypeII_Excerpt_2026.pdf

Happy to join a bridge — propose 11/8 11:00 PST if that works for your team.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Information Security
Redwood Inference
